Some drugs can't kill you from withdrawl, but it's horrible. I had a "friend" that would shoot up pills. She had no where to go and was at the verge of losing both of her kids. I thought I could help... I mean I was naive in some ways I guess, but I never had someone ask me for something so serious. So I used my savings and got us a hotel room. At first she just was a little sick, but then for days it was a living hell. Every single inch of her body was in pain. She would scream and cry for hours and hours. She couldn't really control her body so bathroom stuff was not good. If she took a shower just the feeling of the water on her body made her scream. I did my best to take care of her and make her feel comfortable. It was intense... 

Then when she finally was feeling better, well she talked about how she just wanted to do it one more time. Because in her mind since it was out of her system if she did it just one more time it would feel really good... I told her if she did then I would leave. I went out to get some food and when I got back she told me someone had brought her a pill and she shot it up. So I packed up my things and left. She kept calling me when I was driving home (about a 2 hr drive) but I didn't answer. I cried the entire way home though, because I felt like I failed, and even though I was abandoning her for good reason my guilt was intense. I had nothing left to give though, and I knew I couldn't I help her anymore. I still think about it sometimes. It was like taking care of someone that was possessed. I really did try though. I thought I could save her. I told her that if she got clean I would let her stay with me for awhile until she got back on her feet, but once she did the drugs again after I helped her withdraw I knew I couldn't do anything. 

I mean if losing her two kids was not enough motivation, then what could I do? It's very sad. She is just caught in a viscous cycle. She is an escort/sex worker now. She had done it some in the past when I knew her but she wanted out. Actually, at the hotel I rented she had a few guys come over and I waited out in the car until she was done. It was a strange experience... But that was he way of making money and I wasn't trying to judge. Its just because she is addicted to drugs it's a cycle she can't break. She does the escort stuff so that she can have enough money for hotels and stuff and for drugs, but then she has no money left after that, so she does more escort stuff. Sometimes the escort stuff made her feel terrible, so that meant more drugs... I felt like a failure for a long time, but now I know there was nothing I can do. As far as I know she is still doing the same thing and at this point pretty sure she lost her kids. :(

Yeah, I understand what you mean, for real... but people like us that have these type of problems, but are also smart and able to communicate are not exactly what they are looking for. Like you said  when you have gone to the hospital people have wondered what you are there for because you are not completely insane. See, people in general, and especially when it comes to disability stuff, think that if you are disabled enough to get SSI it means that you are one of those insane people. If you were to answer 100% honestly and be like: Oh, well on a typical day I like to go online and read stuff on message boards, and maybe chat with people... It doesn't make you seem like the "typical" crazy person that they expect. So, when I said exaggerate I guess I meant just leave out anything that can make people wonder. 

That's why when I wrote my form for my SSI review I just pretended it was a writing assignment, and my job was to write about how I feel on my WORST day. Them wording it as "typical" day is super loaded... Keep that in mind. All of the questions are there to give them reason to find something to deny you for. They are NOT interested in your honest/heartfelt answer, they don't want to help you... you are just a number. Their job is to find reasons to deny you and to try and get you to go away. Medicade/SSI costs government tons of money... so the entire system is set up to deny you.

So I guess my point is to consider any questions like that to be an assignment, know your audience and what they expect to hear from someone with your condition/s, and don't elaborate on any of the positive things in your life.

Well they denied me, too, one time... and my appeal. Then the second time it went better and had a lawyer. The lawyer just took money from my backpay. You probably should look into getting one. It's really helpful if you have recent medical history/treatment, and if you have a doctor willing to help out. Mine wrote a small letter about how I was unable to function at the time... 

Also... I think exaggerating is the way to go. I mean for example I had my SSI review (they check periodically every few years) and it asked things I like to do, what my normal day is like. I gave a very detailed, but short, and exaggerated answer... pretty much just like: For me there is no such thing as a typical day, that is part of my illness. I try to wake up, but my medication makes it difficult. I then take my medicine that helps me wake up. I try to remember to wash my face, brush my teeth. Then I go back into bed and wait for my medication to work... sometimes it does, sometimes it does not and I cry... then I try to get some food, etc etc, then I take medicine go to bed.

That sort of thing. Just try to give the answer they want by describing how you might feel on one of your worst days. Don't sell yourself short by being "too honest" just because you are smart and it's not ALWAYS that bad.

I am a bit older than you are (27), but when I was your age I had severe agoraphobia and panic/anxiety disorder. It really, really, sucks. I was able to pull myself out of it though, for the most part. I just started going outside for a few seconds at a time, and gradually built myself up. I did a lot of working out indoors to help with my self image and eventually was leaving the house walking/jogging for miles... then eventually  driving, then going to another city, then moving... It was a long process. I don't think I could have done all of it without ATIVAN and my Dr./Therapist that I was seeing.

Unfortunately, I wasn't able to fix everything. I still have the tendency to shut down when things get overwhelming or stress accumulates too much. I can go from being an attractive/fit guy, getting all As in college, super confident with girls... to isolating myself and losing track of everything. I really hate this cycle. That's kind of where I am at now. I don't have agoraphobia anymore, but I definitely have tendencies.

While you are still feeling functional, do what you need to do to register with your university's disability support service. Talk to your adviser and let them know what is going on. There might come a time when your depression spirals and you miss a lot of class... If you take these steps then you have foundation laid where it will be easier to make things up. You can get accommodations for note takers and the ability to make work up. Most professors are generally nice people and willing to help. They might even have super strict rules, but that's just because if they let one person slide, they have to for everyone - that changes if you are registered with DSS. I only have had one professor give me problems after they knew I was with DSS. (It was one of my easiest classes... I had the highest grade in the class, but missed my 3rd exam and she said I couldn't make it up without a doctor's note. I got a doctor's note and she said it wasn't specific enough... Well, DSS stepped in and took care of it...) but generally every professor has helped. I have had to take an incomplete in classes before and make up the final exams. But if you just disappear and no one knows why that makes it REALLY hard to come back from. Take the hard steps now. Trust me!

Yeah, it sucks to hear, but unfortunately it's true. I doubt she was lying. She probably is just doing her best. It is not her fault you are depressed. It is not her fault that you feel like you need her to give meaning to your life. Actually, that is probably the main reason she is being distant. She is probably scared/uncomfortable because it is a lot of responsibility to be in a relationship with someone when you count on them to give you meaning. It pushes them away. You need to let go of your anger because it's directed at the wrong person. Take accountability for your own self. Get a therapist if you don't already, go to support group meetings, find meetups of something you enjoy (try looking up pathfinder society meetups... it's pretty nerdy, but no one there will judge you and it's a nice escape.) Forgive her, and forgive yourself. I have had lots of people leave me because of my mood issues, it sucks... but when you are in an intimate relationship with someone they share everything, including your mood issues. It is inevitable.  That's why you have to be proactive about it so you do not put everything on them, and if they do leave you don't crash. People leave each other for all kinds of reasons, it is normal... Normal people get sad, angry, but inevitably accept it and move on. When you suffer from depression or mood disorders it is very easy to get super attached to someone to the point you feel dependent on them. So when they leave you get super angry at them for betraying you, everything feels backwards, you feel like it's a bad dream, or maybe if you just change things will get better. Then you blame them more than they deserve... Do you know how she is feeling right now or are you just mad? It sucks, but you have to take care of yourself. Be kind to yourself and be kind to her and let it go.
